title: The Night Guard's Three Rules
rules: lock the front doors at midnight
do not walk down that hall

beats.voiceover: You just landed the easiest museum night-guard gig in town—double pay, zero visitors. Only catch? The manager slides you a sweat-stained card with three rules and won't meet your eyes.
beats.visual: A nervous museum manager slides a worn, sweat-stained rule card under a glowing lobby desk lamp to a new night guard.

beats.voiceover: Rule one: lock the front doors at midnight sharp. Don't crack them open a single inch—even if a lost little kid is crying on the steps outside.
beats.visual: A night guard turns a heavy brass key in the museum's glass entrance while a tiny motionless silhouette stands out in the dark street.

beats.voiceover: Rule two: at two o'clock, every security camera in the long east hall clicks completely black. Do not walk down that hall to check what tripped the breaker.
beats.visual: A row of security monitors goes pitch black at once while a long empty museum hall stretches into dim blue shadow.

beats.voiceover: Rule three: if you hear footsteps matching yours one pace behind you, keep walking straight ahead. Never turn around, and never glance into the tall glass display cases.
beats.visual: A wide-eyed guard walks briskly forward down a dark gallery flanked by gleaming glass display cases, refusing to look left or right.

beats.voiceover: Last month, a cocky rookie laughed it off as hazing. At two o'clock, he grabbed his flashlight and strolled straight down that dark east hall. At three, the security cameras blinked back on. There he stood, frozen like stone—while his own reflection inside the glass case grinned wide, waved goodbye, and walked off on its own. At sunrise, a very cheerful guard clocked out and went home.
beats.visual: Inside a dim hall, a frozen guard stares forward while his own reflection in a glass case grins, waves, and walks the opposite way.

title: Three Rules Cut in the Desk
rules: never climb down the ladder before sunrise

beats.voiceover: Your summer gig sounds like a dream: watching for forest fires alone from a tall wooden tower. Then you spot three rules carved deep into the desk with a hunting knife.
beats.visual: A lone fire lookout traces three deep, fresh lines of carved words across a weathered wooden desk high inside a forest tower.

beats.voiceover: Rule one: before the sun drops, latch every single window tight. Don't stare down at the pines—even when the treetops start swaying furiously with zero wind.
beats.visual: At red sunset, a lookout slams the last wooden tower window shut while dark pine trees sway below under a calm sky.

beats.voiceover: Rule two: never climb down the ladder before sunrise. Stay locked inside the cabin—even if thick smoke curls past the glass or orange flames flicker beneath the stilts.
beats.visual: Faint orange light flickers far below the closed floor hatch while the tense lookout stands motionless beside the top of the ladder.

beats.voiceover: Rule three: after midnight, the emergency radio might crackle on all by itself. Do not answer it—especially when the panicked voice begging for help sounds exactly like yours.
beats.visual: A vintage desk radio glows with a blinking red indicator light in the dark cabin as the lookout watches from across the room.

beats.voiceover: Two weeks ago, a brand-new lookout woke up at three in the morning smelling thick woodsmoke. Convinced the stilts were burning, he threw open the hatch and scrambled down the ladder. At sunrise, the rescue chopper found zero smoke and zero ash. Just his cracked flashlight in the grass—and muddy barefoot prints climbing back up the ladder. They weren't his size.
beats.visual: At sunrise, a shattered flashlight lies in wet grass beneath a tall fire tower beside oversized muddy barefoot prints climbing the ladder.

beats.voiceover: You took the quiet overnight front-desk shift at a tiny roadside hotel. Before sprinting to his car, the old day clerk shoves three rules across the counter with shaking hands.
beats.visual: A pale older hotel clerk with trembling hands shoves a folded sheet of rules across a dim wooden lobby desk to a young night worker.

beats.voiceover: Rule one: after midnight, keep the front door locked tight. Don't let in a polite man holding a brass room key—no matter how warmly he smiles through the glass.
beats.visual: A sharply dressed man holds up a shiny brass key outside a locked glass hotel door at night, flashing an unnaturally wide smile.

beats.voiceover: Rule two: if the elevator dings from the empty top floor, do not go up. Nobody's booked a room up there in twelve years—and the bell always sounds weirdly cheerful.
beats.visual: The brass indicator arrow above a hotel elevator lights up on the top floor while the night clerk stays frozen behind the desk.

beats.voiceover: Rule three: if somebody softly calls your first name from the dark hallway behind the desk, do not answer. Never say your own name out loud until sunrise.
beats.visual: The night clerk sits rigid behind the front desk with wide eyes while the unlit hallway behind the counter stretches completely empty.

beats.voiceover: Last Tuesday, the new night clerk heard someone whisper his name from the shadows by the stairwell. Half-asleep, he leaned over the counter and called back, "Yeah, coming!" When the morning manager unlocked the lobby, the chair sat completely empty—only his plastic name badge rested neatly on the desk. Then, right on cue, the elevator bell dinged once from the top floor.
beats.visual: In pale morning light, an empty hotel desk holds a single plastic name badge as the brass elevator doors silently slide shut.
